shipped_rows.title_o: Weak support for a U-shaped pattern between societal gender equality and fertility when comparing societies across time
shipped_rows.outcome_quote: The analysis identifies a conditional U-shaped relationship between gender equality and fertility

parent_scope_objection: Second and final scoped scientific review, one prior scientific opinion retained in the attempt ceiling. Do not repair the legacy normalized/nonliteral quote or assume a technical inspector has decided correctness. Independent raw primary inspection raised this precise unresolved question: Legacy scientific decision and raw provider wording are preserved, but its nonliteral proof has not yet passed new literal-primary/context inspection. Appendix says the same sources were accessed but original sample could not be matched: 2054 rather than 1993 cumulative years because newer TFR data were included. Existing exact-original-data rationale overstates sample identity. Read the full original-specific Results/Discussion/Conclusion, all earlier source/argument history and codebook. Settle the actual finding/type/identity and any dependent outcome using a short contiguous raw literal passage; distinct passages may be separately recorded, never spliced. The author whole-target synthesis governs over a secondary contrast, but generic theory or other-original support cannot be transferred. Same-source access is not identical sample/data; computational rerun, alternative-specification robustness and new-sample tests must remain separate. If there is an actual primary-source ambiguity or evidence-access limit, identify it exactly; no forced verdict. If original/type remains unresolved, do not transfer a categorical outcome. A removal needs positive target/duplicate evidence, never title/DOI difference alone.

prior_scientific_decisions.quote: Kolk’s (2019) original analysis was based on Stata software; in this study, I try to replicate Kolk’s (2019) finding in R version 4.1.3. Specifically, I replicate Figures 1, 2, and 3 in Kolk’s original paper. My visualisation is based on the ggplot2 package, version 3.4.0. The result of my replication is shown in the Appendix Table A-1 and Figures A-1 to A-3. For the replication, I accessed the same data source as Kolk (2019). For the WPEI, the latest version is version 12, and data from different versions is not comparable. Because the version of data used in the original research was not clearly stated, I tried several versions of the dataset and contacted the V-Dem Institute to gain access to the version 7.1 data used in the original study.
prior_scientific_decisions.reason: Rather than collecting new data in a fresh sample, the study re-analyses Kolk's (2019) historical country-year panel data from the Human Fertility Database and V-Dem version 7.1 in R to verify the original Figures 1-3 and OLS models (Appendix), and then conducts sensitivity/robustness re-analyses on the overlapping 1950-2003 subset of 32 of the 35 original countries by substituting an alternative historical gender equality measure (HGEI) and tempo-adjusted TFR.
